clusters.name: Data Access Abstraction via Repository Pattern
clusters.description: Architectural decisions about abstracting persistence/query logic using repositories. Values differ by which domains are explicitly targeted for repository encapsulation (orders, profiles, meals, promotions, subscriptions).

relations.rationale: UI-driven interaction flows typically depend on structured profile/order/meal access behind repositories.

values.label: Repository for orders, promotions, subscriptions

values.label: Repository for profiles, orders, meals
values.description: Use repositories to encapsulate reads/writes for user profiles, meal orders, and meal data/query operations.

clusters.name: UI Interaction Structure via MVC Pattern
clusters.description: Architectural decisions about structuring user-facing workflows using MVC. Values differ by whether MVC is chosen as the governing UI interaction architecture for core flows.

relations.rationale: MVC UI flows commonly benefit from observing domain state changes (e.g., promotions/subscriptions) to update views.
MVC controllers/views typically call into repository-backed services for interaction-driven reads/writes.

values.label: MVC for user interaction flows

values.label: MVC for core browsing/profile/order modifications
values.description: Use MVC to separate model, view, and controller concerns for browsing meals, profile updates, and order/meal modifications.

clusters.name: Asynchronous State Propagation via Observer Pattern
clusters.description: Architectural decisions about how UI layers learn about state changes asynchronously. Values differ by adopting Observer for propagating promotion/subscription updates into views.

relations.rationale: Observer-driven updates primarily serve view consistency within an MVC-style UI structure.

values.label: Observer for promotion/subscription UI updates
values.description: Use Observer to push promotion/subscription state changes to UI views asynchronously for timely updates.

clusters.name: Catalog Search Constraint Modeling via Specification Pattern
clusters.description: Architectural decisions about how meal search constraints are represented and composed. Values differ by modeling search filters as availability + dietary specifications and supporting multi-vendor catalogs.

relations.rationale: Search specifications typically execute against meal/order/profile data that is abstracted via repositories.

values.label: Availability and dietary filters as specifications
values.description: Implement search filtering as composable specification components for availability and dietary criteria.

values.label: Vendor-agnostic filtering for multi-vendor ghost kitchen
values.description: Ensure specifications operate correctly across items offered by third-party vendors within a shared catalog experience.

clusters.name: Third-Party Provider Integration via Adapter and Strategy
clusters.description: Architectural decisions about integrating heterogeneous external services and swapping algorithms/providers. Values differ by using Adapter for interface unification and Strategy for pluggable provider/search selection.

relations.rationale: Search algorithms/providers often work alongside search constraints to produce final filtered results.

values.label: Adapter for multi-map-provider integration
values.description: Use Adapter to translate each map provider’s interface into a shared common interface for the platform.

values.label: Strategy for swappable map providers/search algorithms
values.description: Use Strategy so different map providers or search algorithms can be exchanged via interchangeable components.

saturation_history.rationale: All open codes map cleanly onto existing taxonomy dimensions: (1) Repository pattern for orders/promotions/subscriptions → Data Access Abstraction (Dimension 1, value 1.1). (2) Repository pattern for profiles/orders/meals → Data Access Abstraction (Dimension 1, value 1.2). (3) MVC architecture for user interaction flows / MVC for core browsing-profile-order modifications → UI Interaction Structure via MVC (Dimension 2, values 2.1/2.2). (4) Observer pattern for asynchronous UI updates on promotion/subscription changes → Asynchronous State Propagation via Observer (Dimension 3, value 3.1). (5) Meal search filters as availability + dietary specifications → Catalog Search Constraint Modeling via Specification Pattern (Dimension 4, value 4.1). (6) Search filtering supports multi-vendor ghost-kitchen catalog → same specification dimension (Dimension 4, value 4.2) capturing vendor-agnostic filtering. (7) Adapter pattern for multi-map-provider integration → Third-Party Provider Integration via Adapter (Dimension 5, value 5.1). (8) Strategy pattern for swappable map providers/search algorithms → same integration dimension (Dimension 5, value 5.2). Therefore, no relevant open concept remains outside the taxonomy’s existing axes of architectural variation.

All relevant open codes are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions: (1) Encrypted credential storage and strict access control for authentication secrets map to Dimension 6 (Credential Security Controls). (2) Standard authentication against stored credentials maps to Dimension 7 (Authentication and Account Verification Workflow Design), and (3) client/server registration validation and (4) registration confirmation after signup are also values within Dimension 7. (5) Facade abstraction for map-provider integration maps directly to Dimension 8. Therefore, there are no uncovered concepts in this minibatch.

dropped_dimensions.rationale: Authentication credential security and secret-handling controls are important generally, but the use case for this step is centered on architectural variation for ghost-kitchen catalog, multi-vendor ordering/discovery, and personalization data flows. None of the provided dimensions in scope explicitly link credential storage/access-control choices to the core architecture decisions being classified.

User account verification workflow (signup validation/confirmation) is orthogonal to the main ghost-kitchen architectural variations in catalog search, provider/vendor integration, pickup mapping, data/persistence abstractions, and recommendation pipeline enablement. It does not meaningfully change the architectural intent described by the included dimensions for this use case.
